optionalSupplies: A flashlight and a warm drink for the camp-style version
substitutes: No lantern? A low lamp in the hall does the job.
title: The Night Watch
clue: Every night, someone in your house does a last check. Tonight it is made official.
reveal: Your dog may already make a last round before bed. Tonight you follow with a quiet 'all is well' at every stop, relieve them of duty at their chosen post, and read the morning report at breakfast.
objective: Follow your dog's own last round at bedtime, mark the post they choose, and read a one-line morning report the next day.
instructions: At dusk, set a small battery lantern or a dimmed lamp in the hall, out of your dog's reach. Lay a blanket at the end of your usual route as the final post. Write 'Watch Log' on a card with room for the date, the stops and the final post. Check the floor and stairs are clear and non-slip.
At your dog's usual last-call time, dim the lights a little. Say nothing and do not call them. Go at their pace and let them lead.

Follow a few steps behind. Wherever they stop, whether a door, a window or a corner, murmur 'all is well' in a low voice. If they skip a door, skip it. There are no wrong turns, and nothing to write yet: just watch.
Let the round end where it ends. If they head straight to bed, the watch is over in a minute and that counts. If they are already asleep, let them sleep and try tomorrow.
At their final post, relieve the watch: crouch nearby, say 'I have the watch' and a quiet goodnight, and offer the blanket if they want it. Turn the lantern off last of all.

The morning report. Next morning, before breakfast, write the Watch Log in one line in your dog's voice ('Doors checked: two. Final post: the radiator. All was well.') and read it aloud once while they stretch or eat.

Pin the log where you pass it each day. On later nights, begin at last night's post and see whether the final post stays the same. After a week, the log is the story of your house at night, told by the one who keeps it.
twist: You are the follower on a round your dog already thinks is their job, and the watch is not over until the morning report is read.
variations: For a dog who has no habit: walk your own short round with them beside you and let them choose the final post.
A camp-style last round: a short dusk loop of the yard or doorstep with a flashlight and a warm drink, dog on a leash, then in to bed. Set your cup down well away from your dog.
For a senior or low-mobility dog: keep the round to one room and sit with them at the final post.
For a new or rescue dog: do it in a single room, with the door of their safe space left open.
completion: Your dog has led the round, even if it was a one-minute check, the lights are out at their chosen post and the morning report is written.
photoIdea: Your dog's silhouette in the lantern light at the final post, with the room dim and calm.
memoryPrompt: Where did your dog stop, and what did the morning report say?
supplies: A battery lantern or small lamp
safety: Use a steady battery light, never a flame, with the battery cover closed and out of reach.
Yard version: keep your dog on a leash and skip it in cold or icy weather.
